title: Agent Harness: Definition
partialText: An agent harness manages a software loop between an AI model and its tools. Its context, permissions, and limits shape what users can do.

title: Usability 101: Introduction to Usability
partialText: Usability refers to how easily people can complete tasks with a design. Improve it by watching representative users do realistic tasks, early and repeatedly.

title: The Role of UX in Agentic Software Factories
partialText: AI-native software development lifecycles reduce UX to AI context. UX must discover user needs, shape what’s built, and evaluate it before and after launch.

title: Experience Design: Dropping the “User” from “User Experience”
partialText: AI is expanding UX beyond human users to agents acting on their behalf. Experience  design names this broader field, which still centers on people’s goals.

title: UX Disciplines: Glossary
partialText: Definitions of fields related to user experience, including UX design, UI design, visual design, interaction design, service design, UX research, and DesignOps

title: AI in UX: Work Is Faster, But Practitioners Have Mixed Feelings
partialText: AI saves UX practitioners time on nearly every task, yet most feel lukewarm about it: mandates, unreliable output, and inflated expectations eat the gains.

title: Synthetic Users vs. Human Respondents: Same Conclusion, Less Variation
partialText: Data from AI-generated respondents pointed to the same conclusion as a survey of 604 humans but contained far fewer distinct answers.

title: UX Maps: Glossary
partialText: Use this glossary to quickly clarify key terms and concepts related to UX maps.

title: The New Siri’s Biggest Strength Is Not Intelligence
partialText: A useful AI assistant needs relevant personal context, the capability to use it, and an experience that helps users understand its limits.

title: Context Libraries: How AI Power Users Manage Context Engineering
partialText: Claude power users rarely edit their context files and often can’t find them. Your AI agent is only as powerful as its context library.

title: Empathy Mapping: The First Step in Design Thinking
partialText: Empathy maps help UX teams visualize user attitudes and behaviors, building a shared understanding of end users while highlighting gaps in existing user data.

title: The New Big Ball of Mud: Why Agentic AI Systems Turn Fragile
partialText: AI makes building nearly free, so users grow agentic systems piecemeal into fragile messes they no longer understand.

partialText: AI-agent power users curate 3 kinds of context: global (across tasks), local (task-specific), and ambient (raw streams like email).

partialText: AI tools make it feasible to build fully interactive prototypes of complex interfaces so you can test them with users earlier in the design process.

title: AI Can Help Write an Article, but It Can’t Stand Behind It
partialText: NN/G uses AI for clarity, formatting, and critique, but humans retain editorial judgment and responsibility for every article.
